A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same R2-G2 research. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures and appendices support comparison, including material relocated or reformatted in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original Bayesian neural network and VAE experiments, including classification results, likelihood bounds, gradient-variance measurements and single-layer VAE results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and additionally reports training-set learning curves for several VAE configurations.

M1.justification: Definition 4.1 and Algorithms 1–2 retain the same conditional-mean projection, conjugate-gradient computation and forward/backward construction. Added explanations and assumption disclosures do not change the estimator's procedure.

E1.justification: Both evaluate BNN classification on MNIST and CIFAR-10, and VAE generative modelling on MNIST, Omniglot and Fashion-MNIST. The added training curves concern existing datasets and tasks.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged: MNIST BNN experiments include RT and LRT, while CIFAR-10 BNN and VAE comparisons use RT (Tables 2, 3 and 5). Newly cited methods are not added experimental baselines.

E3.justification: Splits, dynamic binarisation, Adam with batch size 80, optimisation-step budgets and VAE sampling settings remain unchanged. The added MLP specifications and runtime limits disclose settings for existing experiments rather than establish changed protocols.

E4.justification: Figures 6–10 extend the VAE learning-dynamics analysis from test-only curves to paired training/test trajectories. Existing gradient-variance analyses and the single-layer VAE comparison are retained; no new ablation or robustness intervention appears.

E5.justification: Both versions report five runs and define tabulated error bars as ±1.96 standard errors, using σ/√5. The new checklist reiterates reporting practices without introducing seeds, additional repetitions or statistical tests.

E6.justification: Tables 2, 3 and 5, reported throughputs and existing plotted trajectories are unchanged. Figures 6–10 add training-set results; for example, Figure 10 newly shows an RT training-ELBO dip near 40,000 steps for the three-layer Fashion-MNIST VAE.

T1.justification: v2 explicitly restricts the displayed estimator formulas to independent Gaussian variables and adds rank-based iteration and flop-count reasoning in Appendix F. The central propositions and proofs remain intact. Appendix D largely relocates and elaborates the existing conditional-mean argument.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list retain the same claims: a single-sample Rao-Blackwellised estimator, equivalence with LRT in the stated BNN setting, and improved initial-training outcomes. The conclusion's acknowledgment of sometimes modest gains preserves these claims' scope.

C2.justification: Section 4.3 adds a mechanism explanation connecting LRT's scalar variance inversion to R2-G2's covariance-matrix computation. v2 also clarifies the independence boundary, acknowledges modest gains and identifies low-rank covariance models as an extension example.

D1.justification: Section 5.2 newly specifies two hidden layers of 1024 ReLU units for the MNIST MLP, and Table 4 adds runtime limits. An added footnote explains Algorithm 1's automatic-differentiation construction. The checklist states that experiment code is provided but supplies no code-access location.

R1.justification: v2 adds Glynn (1990), Figurnov et al. (2018) and Tomczak et al. (2020), supporting score-function attribution, reparameterisation discussion and possible low-rank extensions. Positioning relative to LRT and stochastic linear regression remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section sequence are retained. Local terminology and objective descriptions are refined, explanations and footnotes are added, and appendices are reorganised around a relocated conditional-mean discussion, computational-cost section and NeurIPS checklist.

P2.justification: Document-wide NeurIPS reformatting changes typography, the title block, spacing and float placement. Figures 6–10 are redesigned as paired training/test panels, Table 4 replaces its dataset column with runtime limits, and likelihood captions are corrected. This substantially revises the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v2 improves clarity and reproducibility through an explicit independence qualification, architecture and runtime disclosures, corrected captions and additional training trajectories. The central proofs and benchmark findings remain unchanged, so these are limited improvements rather than a substantially stronger empirical contribution.
